description: DRC export-control escalation: from cobalt quotas to a concentrate export ban
verification_status: confirmed - Reuters (via 12+ outlets), StoneX, SMM, IEA; the event was disclosed on 6 August 2026

2026_concentrate_ban.document: inter-ministerial decree dated 29 June 2026, made public on 6 August 2026
2026_concentrate_ban.content: a full ban on exporting copper and cobalt CONCENTRATES (an intermediate product); exports of refined cathodes and metal remain allowed
2026_concentrate_ban.exceptions: the Minister of Mines may grant one-year permits in 'strategic' cases
2026_concentrate_ban.supersedes: the 2023 framework and all exceptions granted under it - operators must re-confirm their export eligibility
2026_concentrate_ban.new_tax: a tax regime on significant by-products with a 55% valuation coefficient, 3-month transition period
2026_concentrate_ban.background: similar restrictions were imposed in 2013, 2019, and 2023 - each time eroded by exceptions; this is the fourth iteration

market_reaction.copper_lme_3m: up 1.8% to $14,369.50/t - the highest since 29 January 2026

real_scale.analyst_conclusion: the immediate effect is limited, since most DRC copper is already exported refined; the main casualty is Kamoa-Kakula (Ivanhoe + Zijin), which accounted for ~389,000 t of the DRC's roughly 605,000 t of concentrate copper in 2025 (about 64%)

escalation_ladder.measure: full cobalt export ban (ARECOMS Decision No. 001/2025)
quota system: 18,125 t for the rest of 2025; 96,600 t/year for 2026-2027
circular requiring 10% royalty prepayment within 48 hours and a compliance certificate before shipment
unused H1-2026 quotas moved into the strategic reserve (announced 29 June, declaration deadline 5 July)
ban on copper and cobalt concentrate exports plus a tax on by-products (55% coefficient)

analogy: a direct parallel to Indonesia, which banned nickel ore exports in 2020 and forced smelter construction domestically; per the Africa Center for Strategic Studies, more than 13 African countries have imposed export restrictions since 2023 to push local processing
constraint: state administrative capacity remains the limiting factor. Actual exports run at 33-50% of allocated quotas due to customs delays and logistics; the July 2026 platform failure put 20,000 t ($1.1bn) at risk
